cex-emg-xs-constant-radius: 1.1 Parametrize the unit sphere away from its seam and poles by $\Phi(\theta,\phi)=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$. The tangent vectors $\Phi_\theta$ and $\Phi_\phi$ are orthogonal, with squared lengths $1$ and $\sin^2\theta$, so the induced metric is $d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$ and its outward area form is $\omega_{S^2}=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. The omitted seam and poles are chart-boundary sets of two-dimensional measure zero. Hence $\int_{S^2}\omega_{S^2}=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi$. The radius-$L$ sphere factor has area form $L^2\omega_{S^2}$ and area $4\pi L^2$. Thus its area-radius function is $R_A=\sqrt{(4\pi L^2)/(4\pi)}=L$ at every $(\tau,z)$. [given, F1, A1, algebra]
cex-emg-xs-nonharmonic-vacuum: For every smooth positive $H$ on an open $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and every $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$, the metric $g_H$ of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] together with the potential $\mathcal A_\sigma=\sigma(H^{-1}-1)dx^0$ gives a geometric electrovac datum of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]], without any harmonicity condition on $H$.
cex-emg-xs-vanishing-scalars: [F2] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] defines the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations and curvature convention.
def-emg-xs-br-products: The smooth field $N=(L\sqrt{f})^{-1}\partial_\tau$ is unit timelike; it selects the future direction. This explicit metric-field tuple is the **Bertotti-Robinson product data** for this library. “Electrovac” refers to the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and is not asserted by this definition. The product has sphere radius $L$ at every base point.
def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac:
Write $\mathcal I_S$ for [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]]: for a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_j)$ and connected charts $\phi_j$, it sets $\mathcal I_S(\omega)=\sum_j I_{\phi_j}(\rho_j\omega)$, where $I_{\phi_j}$ is the signed chart integral of the compactly supported coefficient. Only finitely many terms are nonzero. The value is independent of charts, partition and refinement by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]]. Define the surface notation by
$$\int_S\eta:=\mathcal I_S(i^*\eta).$$
This agrees with [[prop-integration-over-an-oriented-embedded-submanifold]]; under an orientation-preserving smooth reparametrization $F:T\to S$, the same value is $\mathcal I_T((iF)^*\eta)$.
The integration definition and its independence theorem assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, already retained in the geometric background below. For $\eta=\mathcal F$ and $\eta=\star_g\mathcal F$, smoothness of the given field and Hodge map makes both pulled-back top forms admissible; their integrals are finite real numbers. Define the geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.
def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp: The **positive harmonic conformastatic electrovac data** are the tuple $(\mathcal M,g_H,N_H,o,\mathcal F_\sigma)$ for these choices. The metric is the chart tensor of [[def-emg-conformastatic-chart-data]] and is Lorentzian with the stated future direction by [[lem-emg-conformastatic-chart-is-lorentzian]]. The term “electrovac data” names a candidate for the equations in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; this definition by itself does not assert that the equations hold. The field components have inverse-length units in length coordinates, so the Ricci and quadratic-field components both have inverse-length-squared units.
def-emg-xs-kn-data: Use the smooth covariant metric and signature conventions of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the smooth real form spaces $\Omega^k(U)$ of [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. Geometric electric flux-length normalization means the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; its field equations are not hypotheses in this coordinate definition.
def-emg-xs-null-wave: The vector field $N=\partial_u+\frac{P+1}{2}\partial_v$ has $g(N,N)=-1$ and selects the future direction. The $u,v$ block of $g$ has determinant $-1$, so together with the two positive transverse directions this is a smooth Lorentzian metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\sqrt{|\det g|}=1$. The tuple $(\mathbb R^4,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ is the **null-wave candidate data** for the equations of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]; no field-equation claim is part of this definition. The metric coefficients are dimensionless, and $\mathcal F_{ui}$ has inverse-length units.
def-emg-xs-si-parameters: Use the SI quantities, coordinate convention, and primitive/derived distinction of [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and the zero-cosmological-constant geometric electrovac flux normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. This definition is the model-local parameter map for the RN and KN ansatz families; it is not a claim that nature contains an object with these parameters.

For the geometric flux integrals below, retain the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention explicitly stated by [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] and defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. No arbitrary-index choice principle or magnetic-charge quantization is added.
The SI electric-flux convention is $Q_e=\varepsilon_0c\int_S\star_gF$, and the magnetic quantity used here is the flux $\Phi_B=\int_S F$. Thus

ex-emg-xs-rn-charge-sign: [F4] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] defines sphere flux by pulling back the smooth field or its Hodge dual along a smooth embedding of a compact oriented sphere and integrating the resulting top form. The integral uses the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention; the flux parameter is the integral divided by $4\pi$.

2.1 At fixed $x^0$ and admitted radius $r>0$, the sphere map $u\mapsto(x^0,r,u)$ from the oriented unit sphere into the RN product is a smooth embedding; it is a product-factor inclusion, so it is injective with injective differential and has the continuous inverse given by the sphere projection. The source sphere is compact and has no boundary, and the fields are smooth on a neighborhood since $r>0$ and $f(r)\ne0$. Thus its pulled-back field and dual are smooth compactly supported top forms, and the flux integrals below are the well-defined operation in [F4]. The two fields are $\mathcal F_\pm=\mp\ell r^{-2}dx^0\wedge dr$, so $\mathcal F_-=-\mathcal F_+$. If $f>0$, use the positively oriented coframe $e^0=\sqrt f\,dx^0$, $e^1=f^{-1/2}dr$, $e^2=r\,d\theta$, $e^3=r\sin\theta\,d\phi$. If $f<0$, use $e^0=(-f)^{-1/2}dr$, $e^1=-(-f)^{1/2}dx^0$, $e^2=r\,d\theta$, $e^3=r\sin\theta\,d\phi$. In both cases $dx^0\wedge dr=e^0\wedge e^1$ and $e^2\wedge e^3=r^2\omega_{S^2}$, so [F2] gives $\star_g(dx^0\wedge dr)=-r^2\omega_{S^2}$ and $\star_g\mathcal F_\pm=\pm\ell\,\omega_{S^2}$. For the explicit sphere parametrization $s(\theta,\phi)=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$, differentiation gives $s\cdot(s_\theta\times s_\phi)=\sin\theta$, so the outward form pulls back to $\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$, as in [F1]. The sine density is continuous, hence integrable by [F3]; its primitive is $-\cos\theta$. Its integral on $\delta\le\theta\le\pi-\delta$, $0\le\phi\le2\pi$ is $4\pi\cos\delta$, and the two omitted caps have total area $4\pi(1-\cos\delta)\to0$ by the same bounded polar density; the seam has zero width in the azimuthal integral. Thus $\int_{S^2}\omega_{S^2}=2\pi[-\cos\theta]_0^\pi=4\pi$. The normalized oriented electric sphere fluxes are therefore $(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{S_r}\star_g\mathcal F_\pm=\pm\ell$. Thus the metric does not determine the sign of the electric flux parameter. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
ex-emg-xs-topological-charge: [F1] [[prop-emg-xs-rn-local-gauges]]: the current A-page item proves $\int_{S_r}\mathcal F=4\pi q_m$ and gives smooth local north/south potentials. Its proof is directly supplied using RN data, Hodge calculus and finite-chain Stokes.

1.1 In RN, [F1] gives
$\int_{S_r}\mathcal F=4\pi q_m\ne0$. If $S_r=\partial c$ for a finite
smooth singular 3-chain in the field domain, then $d\mathcal F=0$ by the
local potential identities in [F1] and $d^2=0$. Applying [F2] would give
$$4\pi q_m=\int_{S_r}\mathcal F=\int_c d\mathcal F=0,$$
a contradiction. Thus $S_r$ is nonbounding. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

1.2 Under the exact conditional interface [L1], the chosen $\beta$ gives $\int_{S_r}\mathcal F_\beta=4\pi q\sin\beta\ne0$ and $d\mathcal F_\beta=0$ on the annulus. If a sphere there bounded a finite smooth singular 3-chain, [F2] would force its flux to be zero; if it had a global potential, the closed-cycle Stokes identity would likewise force zero flux. Both contradict [L1]. Hence the KN sphere is nonbounding and has no global potential, conditional on that draft interface. [L1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 If a global smooth potential $\mathcal A$ existed, then [F2] and
$\partial S_r=0$ would give
$$4\pi q_m=\int_{S_r}d\mathcal A=\int_{\partial S_r}\mathcal A=0,$$
contradicting step 1.1's nonzero flux. The smooth patch potentials in [F1]
show that the obstruction is global exactness, not local existence.
[F1, F2, step 1.1, A1, algebra]

prop-emg-xs-kn-dyonic-flux: 1.1 On the sphere let $X=\sin\theta\cos\phi$ and $Y=\sin\theta\sin\phi$. Then $\lambda=X\,dY-Y\,dX=\sin^2\theta\,d\phi$ away from the poles, and [F3] proves this is a global smooth one-form. At a fixed $(x^0,r)$, represent $S_r$ by the oriented radial projections of the eight octahedral faces; each projection extends smoothly to a neighborhood of its face, shared edges cancel, and the resulting finite smooth singular two-chain has zero boundary. The global potential $\bar{\mathcal A}=-qr\Sigma^{-1}(dx^0-a\lambda)$ is smooth since $\Sigma>0$. Hence $\bar{\mathcal F}=d\bar{\mathcal A}$ and [F5] gives $\int_{S_r}\bar{\mathcal F}=\int_{\partial S_r}\bar{\mathcal A}=0$. [F1, F3, F5, A1, construct, algebra]

1.2 For the explicit unit-sphere parametrization $s(\theta,\phi)=(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$, direct differentiation gives $s\cdot(s_\theta\times s_\phi)=\sin\theta$. Thus its outward area form pulls back to $\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. By [F4], the continuous sine density is integrable and its primitive $-\cos\theta$ evaluates each polar integral. Integrating on $\delta\le\theta\le\pi-\delta$, $0\le\phi\le2\pi$ gives $4\pi\cos\delta$; the two caps have total area $4\pi(1-\cos\delta)$ by the same bounded polar density, tending to zero. Hence $\int_{S^2}\omega=4\pi$. In the oriented $(x^0,r,\theta,\phi)$ coordinates, direct raising of $\mathcal F_{r0}=q(r^2-a^2y^2)/\Sigma^2$ and $\mathcal F_{r\phi}=-a\sin^2\theta\,\mathcal F_{r0}$ with the KN inverse metric gives $$(\star_g\mathcal F)_{\theta\phi} =\frac{q(r^2+a^2)(r^2-a^2y^2)\sin\theta}{\Sigma^2} =q\sin\theta+O(r^{-2})\sin\theta,$$ The numerator factor minus $\Sigma^2$ is $a^2r^2(1-3y^2)-a^4y^2(1+y^2)$, whose absolute value is at most $2a^2r^2+2a^4$ for $|y|\le1$. Since $\Sigma^2\ge r^4$, the remainder is uniformly $O(r^{-2})$ on the sphere. Hence $\lim_{r\to\infty}(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{S_r}\star_g\mathcal F=q$. [F1, F4, A1, algebra]

2.1 For $R_0<r_1<r_2$, in the fixed-$x^0$ slice of step 1.1, take the product of each of the same eight projected triangular faces with $[r_1,r_2]$. Each triangular prism splits into three tetrahedra; their oriented sum is a finite smooth singular three-chain $\mathcal C$, internal faces cancel, and its boundary is $S_{r_2}-S_{r_1}$. By steps 1.1-1.2 and [F1], $d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$ on this shell. Stokes [F5] therefore gives $$\int_{S_{r_2}}\star_g\mathcal F-\int_{S_{r_1}}\star_g\mathcal F=\int_{\partial\mathcal C}\star_g\mathcal F=\int_\mathcal C d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0.$$ Step 1.2 identifies the common value as $4\pi q$. [F1, F3, F5, A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]
prop-emg-xs-mp-extremal-rn: [F4] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] fixes the geometric Ricci equation $\operatorname{Ric}=2Q(\mathcal F)$ used to identify the common field data.
prop-emg-xs-mp-multicenter: Then $H$ is smooth, positive and Euclidean harmonic on $D$, so [[def-emg-xs-harmonic-mp]] and [[thm-emg-xs-mp-verification]] give a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum on $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times D$. For each $A$, every coordinate sphere $S_A(r)=\{x:|x-a_A|=r\}$ whose closed ball contains no other center has electric flux $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$ and magnetic flux $q_m(S_A(r))=0$. If a coordinate sphere $S_R=\{x:|x|=R\}$ strictly encloses all centers, its fluxes are $q_e(S_R)=\sigma\sum_A m_A$ and $q_m(S_R)=0$. No center is included in the manifold; these are fluxes through regular spheres, not matter-source, horizon-extension, stability, or completeness claims.
[F3] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] defines $q_e(S)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F$ and $q_m(S)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_S\mathcal F$ for oriented embedded spheres.
[F3] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] defines $q_e(S)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F$ and $q_m(S)=(4\pi)^{-1}\int_S\mathcal F$ for oriented embedded spheres.

1.2 Inverting the diagonal metric in [F1] gives $g^{00}=-H^2$ and $g^{ij}=H^{-2}\delta^{ij}$, so raising $\mathcal F_{i0}=-\sigma H_i/H^2$ gives $\mathcal F^{i0}=\sigma H_i/H^2$. The metric determinant is $(-H^{-2})(H^2)^3=-H^4$, so the oriented volume form is $\mathrm{vol}_g=H^2dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. The Hodge formula [F4] therefore gives $(\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma)_{ij}=-\sigma\epsilon_{ijk}H_k$. Evaluating this two-form on an outward-oriented Euclidean sphere gives $\int_S\star_g\mathcal F_\sigma=-\sigma\int_S\partial_\nu H\,dS_\delta$, because $\partial_\nu H=n^kH_k$ and the induced oriented area form has components $\epsilon_{ijk}n^k dS_\delta$. The pullback of $\mathcal F_\sigma$ to each spatial sphere is zero because every term in [F1] contains $dx^0$, which vanishes on its tangent vectors; hence $q_m(S)=0$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

1.3 Let $S_r(a)$ be a Euclidean sphere with center $a$ and radius $r$, and let $m/|x-b|$ be one term in $H$, where $d:=|b-a|\ne r$. At $x=a+rn$ with $n\in S^2$, its outward normal derivative is $-m(r-n\cdot(b-a))/|rn-(b-a)|^3$. The sphere area element is $r^2d\Omega$, where $d\Omega=\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi$ and $\int_{S^2}d\Omega=2\pi\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta=4\pi$. If $d=0$, direct integration gives flux $-4\pi m$. If $d>0$, choose the polar axis along $b-a$; this orthogonal change preserves the induced sphere area. With $u=\cos\theta$ and $n\cdot(b-a)=du$, the flux is $-2\pi mr^2J$, where $$J:=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{r-du}{(r^2+d^2-2rdu)^{3/2}}\,du.$$ Set $w=r^2+d^2-2rdu$. Then $du=-dw/(2rd)$, the endpoint square roots for $w$ are $r+d$ and $|r-d|$, and $r-du=(r^2-d^2+w)/(2r)$. Therefore $$J=\frac1{4r^2d}\left((r^2-d^2)\int_{(r-d)^2}^{(r+d)^2}w^{-3/2}\,dw+\int_{(r-d)^2}^{(r+d)^2}w^{-1/2}\,dw\right).$$ Using antiderivatives $-2w^{-1/2}$ and $2w^{1/2}$ gives $$J=\frac{(r^2-d^2)\bigl(|r-d|^{-1}-(r+d)^{-1}\bigr)+(r+d-|r-d|)}{2r^2d}.$$ If $d<r$, the numerator is $4d$, so $J=2/r^2$; if $d>r$, the numerator is $0$, so $J=0$. Thus a Coulomb term contributes $-4\pi m$ to the outward flux exactly when its center lies inside the sphere, and zero when its center lies outside. [given, algebra]

2.2 For an isolated sphere $S_A(r)$, its own center has $d=0$, while each other center has distance $d_{AB}>r$ by [A1]. Applying step 1.3 term by term gives $\int_{S_A(r)}\partial_\nu H\,dS_\delta=-4\pi m_A$. Step 1.2 yields $q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A$, and that step also gives $q_m(S_A(r))=0$. [given, A1, F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 On an outer sphere that strictly encloses every center, each term has $d=|a_A|<R$. Step 1.3 gives $\int_{S_R}\partial_\nu H\,dS_\delta=-4\pi\sum_A m_A$. Step 1.2 therefore yields $q_e(S_R)=\sigma\sum_A m_A$ and $q_m(S_R)=0$. [given, A1, F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎
prop-emg-xs-null-invariants: If $a(u_0)^2+b(u_0)^2>0$ at any $u_0$, then the Riemann tensor is nonzero there; the metric is not flat. Here $R_{abcd}$ and $S$ use the convention in [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]].
[F3] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] fixes the curvature sign, Ricci contraction, and scalar contraction used here.
pthm-emg-xs-dyonic-model:
Take a pure-electric KN seed with SI inputs $m_*>0$, $J\in\mathbb R$ and $Q_0\in\mathbb R$, zero magnetic flux, and parameters
$$M=\frac{G_Nm_*}{c^2},\qquad a=\frac{J}{m_*c},\qquad q_0=\gamma_e Q_0,\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad \gamma_e:=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}.$$
For a fixed real duality angle $\beta$, rotate its geometric field by
$$\mathcal F_\beta:=\cos\beta\,\mathcal F_0+\sin\beta\,\star_g\mathcal F_0,$$
where $\mathcal F_0=\alpha F_0$ is the seed's geometric field. On the seed's
stated Boyer–Lindquist domains, the dual-rotated geometric field is source-free
and has unchanged geometric stress, conditional on [[lem-emg-xs-duality]];
thus $F_\beta:=\mathcal F_\beta/\alpha$ and the same metric solve the same
equation-based SI model, conditional on [[pthm-emg-xs-kn-model]]. On the
full-sphere exterior $\mathcal X:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(R_0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ of [[def-emg-xs-kn-full-sphere-exterior]], with $R_0>4|M|$, the
resulting geometric flux parameters and matching SI inputs are
$$q_e=q_0\cos\beta,\qquad q_m=q_0\sin\beta,\qquad Q_e^{\mathrm{out}}=Q_0\cos\beta,\qquad \Phi_B^{\mathrm{out}}=\mu_0cQ_0\sin\beta.$$
In particular $q_e^2+q_m^2=q_0^2$, so the metric is unchanged. On each sphere-containing full-sphere exterior region, $\int_{S_r}\mathcal F_\beta=4\pi q_m$; hence a global smooth real one-form potential for $\mathcal F_\beta$ there is impossible if $q_m\ne0$, by finite-chain Stokes. In the nonrotating case $a=0$, the corresponding dyonic RN field also has the explicit north/south patch potentials and exact global-potential criterion of [[prop-emg-xs-rn-local-gauges]]. No charge quantization, ADM/Komar identification or observed object is asserted.

2.2 On the full-sphere exterior [F8], let $y=\cos\theta$, $\Sigma=r^2+a^2y^2$, and $R=r^2+a^2$. Differentiating the exact seed potential in [F2] gives $(\mathcal F_0)_{r0}=q_0(r^2-a^2y^2)/\Sigma^2$ and $(\mathcal F_0)_{r\phi}=-a\sin^2\theta(\mathcal F_0)_{r0}$. Raising indices with the KN inverse metric and applying [F7] yields $(\star_g\mathcal F_0)_{\theta\phi}=q_0R(r^2-a^2y^2)\sin\theta/\Sigma^2$. Since $\frac{d}{dy}(y/\Sigma)=(r^2-a^2y^2)/\Sigma^2$, integration over the outward sphere gives
$$\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S_r}\star_g\mathcal F_0=\frac{q_0R}{2}\int_{-1}^1\frac{r^2-a^2y^2}{(r^2+a^2y^2)^2}\,dy=\frac{q_0R}{2}\left[\frac{y}{\Sigma}\right]_{-1}^1=q_0.$$
The global potential in [F8] and Stokes' theorem [F5] give $\int_{S_r}\mathcal F_0=\int_{S_r}d\mathcal A_0=0$. By [F7], $\star_g^2=-1$ on two-forms, so integrating $\mathcal F_\beta=\cos\beta\,\mathcal F_0+\sin\beta\star_g\mathcal F_0$ and its Hodge dual directly yields $q_e=q_0\cos\beta$ and $q_m=q_0\sin\beta$. Therefore $q_e^2+q_m^2=q_0^2(\cos^2\beta+\sin^2\beta)=q_0^2$, and every KN metric coefficient depending on charge through this sum is unchanged. This local integral calculation proves the stated flux values. [F2, F5, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.2 Assume a global smooth real one-form $\mathcal A_\beta$ on a sphere-containing exterior with $d\mathcal A_\beta=\mathcal F_\beta$ and $q_m\ne0$. Represent the fixed sphere $S_r$ by radially projecting the eight oriented triangular faces of the octahedron onto the unit sphere and taking their signed sum. Each face is disjoint from the origin, so its radial projection is smooth; common edges cancel with opposite orientations. This is a finite smooth singular $2$-cycle, so $\partial S_r=0$. By [F5] and step 2.2,
$$4\pi q_m=\int_{S_r}\mathcal F_\beta=\int_{S_r}d\mathcal A_\beta=\int_{\partial S_r}\mathcal A_\beta=0,$$
a contradiction. Thus no such global potential exists on the rotating sphere-containing exterior when its magnetic flux is nonzero. [F5, step 2.2, algebra]
pthm-emg-xs-geometric-to-si-model:
Let $(M,g,N,o,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth source-free geometric electrovac datum
of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on a nonempty smooth four-manifold.
Thus $g$ has signature $(-,+,+,+)$, $\mathcal F$ is a smooth real two-form,
and
$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F),\qquad Q_{ab}(X):=X_{ac}X_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}X_{cd}X^{cd}.$$
Choose constants $G_N,c,\mu_0>0$ in the SI roles of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]], set
$$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1},\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{\frac{4\pi G_N}{\mu_0c^4}},\qquad F:=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F,$$
and use the same metric and orientation for $F$. In length coordinates
$x^0=ct$, $F_{ab}$ has units T, $\mathcal F_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$,
and $\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{T}^{-1}\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ by
[[def-emg-xs-si-parameters]]. Define
$$T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}Q_{ab}(F),\qquad \kappa_E:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}.$$
In the adopted postulate [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]], specialize
to $\Lambda=0$, $j=0$, and $T^m=0$. Then
$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla^g_aF^{ab}=0,\qquad G_{ab}=\kappa_E T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}.$$
This is a conditional model deduction: it neither derives the postulate nor
claims that the model describes nature.

[F1] [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]: the geometric datum has smooth $\mathcal F$, signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and equations $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$ and $\operatorname{Ric}=2Q(\mathcal F)$, with the displayed trace-free quadratic tensor.
pthm-emg-xs-mp-model:
$$\overline B_A(r):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x-a_A|\le r\}.$$
Orient $S_A(r)$ by its outward unit normal relative to the standard orientation
of $\mathbb R^3$.
Whenever $\overline B_A(r)$ contains no other center, the geometric fluxes are
$$q_e(S_A(r))=\sigma m_A,\qquad q_m(S_A(r))=0.$$
The corresponding SI electric-flux parameter is
$$Q_{e,A}:=\varepsilon_0c\int_{S_A(r)}\star_gF =\sigma\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}\,m_{*,A},$$
and its magnetic flux $\int_{S_A(r)}F$ is zero. Define the outward-oriented
origin-centered sphere by $S_R:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=R\}$, where the
orientation is induced by the outward unit normal relative to the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$. For $R>\max_A|a_A|$, it has
the sum of these electric fluxes. These
are model parameters and regular-sphere fluxes, not measurements or evidence
of regular material sources at the removed points.
pthm-emg-xs-rn-horizons: 2.2 For $Q^2>0$ and $M^2\ge Q^2$, [L1] gives the claimed root crossing and, when $M^2>Q^2$, the local bifurcation chart. If $Q^2=M^2$, [L1] gives the regular ingoing crossing but explicitly does not assert that simple-root chart. For $Q^2=0$, put $r_H=2M$, $\kappa=1/(4M)$, and write $f=(r-r_H)b(r)$ with $b(r)=1/r$ and $b(r_H)=2\kappa>0$. Then $$\frac1f-\frac1{2\kappa(r-r_H)}=\frac{2\kappa-b(r)}{2\kappa b(r)(r-r_H)}=-\frac1{2\kappa b(r)}\int_0^1b'(r_H+s(r-r_H))\,ds,$$ so this difference extends smoothly across $r_H$. Integrate it to $h$ with $h(r_H)=0$, and define $K(r)=(r-r_H)\ell_*^{-1}e^{2\kappa h(r)}$. Then $K'(r_H)=\ell_*^{-1}>0$ and differentiation gives $fK'=2\kappa K$ on both sides and at the root. By [F3], shrink the radial interval so $K'>0$ and $K$ has a smooth local inverse $\rho$ about zero. On the selected ingoing model define $$V=e^{\kappa v},\qquad U=-K(r)e^{-\kappa v}.$$ Thus $UV=-K(r)$, with $U<0$ for $r>r_H$ and $U>0$ for $r<r_H$, and the Jacobian is $\kappa K'(r)>0$ across the root. The inverse is $r=\rho(-UV)$ and $v=\kappa^{-1}\log V$ on $V>0$. Differentiating gives $dv=dV/(\kappa V)$ and $dr=-(V\,dU+U\,dV)/K'(r)$. Substitution in the original ingoing block $-f\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr$ cancels its $dV^2$ coefficient by $fK'=2\kappa K$, leaving $$-\frac1{\kappa K'(\rho(-UV))}(dU\otimes dV+dV\otimes dU).$$ This coefficient is smooth and nonzero, and the sphere term is $\rho(-UV)^2\gamma$. Choose $\varepsilon>0$ so these formulas are defined with $\rho(-UV)>0$ on $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)^2$. They give a smooth Lorentzian metric on the full rectangle times $S^2$, agreeing with the selected ingoing metric on its entire $V>0$ half, including both $r<r_H$ and $r>r_H$. Glue that half to its old coordinate preimage. Any overlap sequence tending to a new point on $V=0$ has $v=\kappa^{-1}\log V\to-\infty$, so cannot approach a finite old point; the other rectangle edges are not new points. This gives a Hausdorff local extension. The field is zero in this uncharged case. The old Killing field becomes $\kappa(V\partial_V-U\partial_U)$; it extends smoothly, preserves the displayed metric, is null and normal on either axis away from their intersection, and vanishes on the spacelike sphere $U=V=0$. Thus this is the required two-sided local bifurcation chart. [L1, F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra, construct]
texp-emg-xs-null-curvature:
Choose a constant $\nu>0$ with units $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ and the profiles
$a(u)=\nu$, $b(u)=0$, $h(u,x,y)=0$ in
[[def-emg-xs-null-wave]]. Then
$$P=-\nu^2(x^2+y^2),\qquad g=-2\,du\,dv+dx^2+dy^2-\nu^2(x^2+y^2)du^2,$$
$$\mathcal F=\nu\,du\wedge dx,\qquad F=\alpha^{-1}\mathcal F.$$
Use orientation $du\wedge dv\wedge dx\wedge dy$ and future unit field
$N=\partial_u+(P+1)\partial_v/2$ from the null-wave definition. This is a smooth source-free solution of the adopted SI model of
[[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] by
[[pthm-emg-xs-null-wave-model]]. Its electromagnetic field is nonzero.
Define the scalar curvature by $S:=g^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, using the
curvature convention of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. Then
$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=0,\qquad S=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\operatorname{Ric}^{ab}=0,\qquad R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=0.$$
At the same time $R_{uxux}=\nu^2\ne0$, so the spacetime is not flat. These
zero scalar contractions therefore do not imply a vanishing electromagnetic
field or flat spacetime. This is a hypothetical model calculation, not an
observation.

thm-emg-xs-rn-crossing:
5.1 On each quadrant $UV\ne0$, define
$$t:=\frac{1}{2\kappa}\log\left|\frac VU\right|,\qquad r=\rho(-UV).$$
These are smooth coordinates there: $r=\rho(-UV)$ and the logarithmic ratio
independently determine the product and quotient of the nonzero coordinates,
so their Jacobian is nonzero. Differentiating gives
$$dr=-\frac{V\,dU+U\,dV}{K'(r)},\qquad dt=\frac{1}{2\kappa}\left(\frac{dV}{V}-\frac{dU}{U}\right),\qquad dt\wedge dr=\frac{1}{\kappa K'(r)}dU\wedge dV.$$
Put $\alpha=dU/U$ and $\eta=dV/V$. Since $UV=-K(r)$, the displayed
differentials give $dr=(K/K')(\alpha+\eta)$ and
$dt=(\eta-\alpha)/(2\kappa)$. Substituting in the static radial metric
$-fdt^2+f^{-1}dr^2$ of [F1], and using $fK'=2\kappa K$ from step 2.1,
the $\alpha\otimes\alpha$ and $\eta\otimes\eta$ coefficients cancel
and each cross coefficient is $f/(2\kappa^2)=K/(\kappa K')$. Therefore
the radial tensor is
$$\frac{K}{\kappa K'}(\alpha\otimes\eta+\eta\otimes\alpha) =-\frac1{\kappa K'}(dU\otimes dV+dV\otimes dU),$$
using $K=-UV$. The sphere term remains $r^2\gamma$. The two-form satisfies
$-q_e r^{-2}dt\wedge dr+q_m\omega
=-q_e(\kappa r^2K')^{-1}dU\wedge dV+q_m\omega$, exactly its expression
from step 4.1. Thus each quadrant is a static RN chart with $f\ne0$.
Since $\kappa K'(r)>0$, its orientation agrees with
$dt\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. The exact static-domain interface [L1] makes
the geometric Einstein and Maxwell residuals vanish on all four quadrants.
The metric, field and inverse metric are smooth on the full extension chart,
so the residual tensors are continuous; a continuous tensor vanishing on a
dense subset vanishes on its closure. This proves the stated conditional
equation extension to both axes and the bifurcation sphere.
[F1, L1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]
thm-emg-xs-rn-escape:
1.2 Fix $r_0>r_H$, $v_0\in\mathbb R$, and $\omega_0\in S^2$. For
$r\ge r_0$, set
$$v(r)=v_0+\int_{r_0}^r\frac{2}{f(s)}\,ds.$$
Here $f(s)=(s-r_+)(s-r_-)/s^2>0$ because $s>r_+$, so [F4] gives
$v'(r)=2/f(r)$. The curve $\gamma(r)=(v(r),r,\omega_0)$ has tangent
$$\gamma'(r)=\frac{2}{f(r)}\partial_v+\partial_r =\frac{2}{f(r)}n,$$
a positive multiple of the future null field in [F1]. Reparameterize by $s=r-r_0\in[0,\infty)$ to obtain the path domain in [L1]. It is defined for
every finite $r\ge r_0$ and therefore reaches arbitrarily large radii in
the exact path sense of [L1]. Every point with $r>r_H$ lies in $\mathcal E$.
[F1, F4, L1, A1, algebra]
